title: DBMS Flashcards
subject: dbms
description: Flip-card revision for DBMS — normalization, keys, transactions, indexing, and SQL fundamentals for C-CAT exam preparation and quick recall.

cards.front: Can a Primary Key be NULL?
cards.back: No, never — uniqueness and non-NULL are its two defining constraints

cards.front: Difference between Super Key and Candidate Key
cards.back: Every candidate key is a super key, but a candidate key is minimal — no redundant attributes
Atomic values only, no repeating groups
Partial dependency — a non-key attribute depending on only part of a composite key
Transitive dependency — a non-key attribute depending on another non-key attribute

cards.front: GRANT and REVOKE belong to which SQL category?
Which SQL category includes INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE?
Atomicity vs Durability — what's the difference?
cards.back: Atomicity = all-or-nothing DURING execution. Durability = stays saved AFTER commit, survives crashes

cards.front: How many clustered indexes can a table have?
cards.back: Only 1 — it determines the physical storage order of the table's rows

cards.front: In Two-Phase Locking, what happens right after the first lock release?
cards.back: The transaction enters the shrinking phase and cannot acquire any new locks

cards.front: What does a LEFT JOIN return?
cards.back: All rows from the left table, with NULLs for right-table columns where there's no match

cards.front: B+ Tree vs B-Tree — which do most real databases actually use for indexing?
cards.back: B+ Tree — all data lives at the leaf level, and leaves are linked for efficient range scans
One computed from another attribute — e.g. Age from Date of Birth — not stored directly

cards.front: What does a Foreign Key do?
cards.back: References a Primary Key in another table, enforcing referential integrity between them
